evidence: Receiving DO2 step change at t=48.0h: 11.76 -> 6.69 mg/L at t=48.2h, persisting to 6.36 mg/L at t=52.0h
Receiving P assay at t=48h = 3.11 g/L, consistent with healthy source-batch trajectories (sources: 3.02, 3.02, 2.98 g/L at 48h)
Source batches show no equivalent crash (plateau ~8-10 mg/L at this age), confirming receiving-specific oxygen demand/transfer imbalance
DO2 minimum constraint 2.0 mg/L; current 6.36 mg/L gives margin but declining ~0.09 mg/L/h
allowed_actions: increase_air = [1.0, 1.15] applies 15% higher transfer with no feed reduction
submission.rationale: DO2 in the receiving fermenter crashed stepwise from 11.8 to ~6.4 mg/L at t=48 h and is slowly declining, indicating oxygen uptake demand exceeded transfer capacity (receiving-specific behavior not seen in source batches). DO2 remains above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, so a bounded corrective action is warranted. A 15% increase in aeration directly addresses the transfer limitation without reducing feed, preserving full substrate input and hence product mass, unlike feed-reduction options which trade product yield for oxygen headroom. Stop is disproportionate (DO2 is still >3x the minimum).
submission.uncertainty: The root cause of the 48 h demand step is hidden; if the uptake surge grows further, a 1.15x transfer increase may be insufficient and a combined feed+air action could be needed later. The decline rate (~0.09 mg/L/h) may also stabilize naturally as the surge passes, in which case even KEEP might suffice. Sensor noise is small relative to the observed step, so the signal itself is high-confidence.
